title: Polynomial time for Word RAM decision
statement: Let $P$ be an extended Word RAM program and $L$ a language of Boolean strings. Suppose functions $W,T_W,S_W:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ are such that a finite Turing machine computes $W(n)$ in at most $T_W(n)$ steps and uses at most $S_W(n)$ space. Let $C,d\in\mathbb{N}$, and suppose $T_W(n)+W(n)\le C(n+1)^d$ for every $n$. Suppose also that for every input $x$ there are natural numbers $t,f$ and an output string $o$ with $t\le C(|x|+1)^d$, such that $P$ halts within $t$ steps at word width $W(|x|)$, outputs the Boolean indicator of membership of $x$ in $L$, and uses at most $f$ touched addresses. Then $L$ belongs to polynomial time, that is, $L\in\bigcup_{r\in\mathbb{N}}\mathrm{DTIME}(n^r+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: An extended Word RAM program $P$ and Boolean language $L$
